samira (nb-support): Hey team — Northbridge is seeing intermittent tail latency spikes on our Dedicated-XL pool last night. p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~420ms for a few hours. Can we get a dedicated token_budget/queue_limit tune? Customer is anxious.

dylan: Do you have any examples/traces? Any change in request distribution or prompt lengths? Also curious about KV cache hit rate.

samira (nb-support): Pasting a small excerpt from the logs we pulled, timestamps redacted: 
```
2026-03-14T03:12:21Z route=northbridge-dedicated batch_formed=3 batch_wait_ms=50 kernel=generic_attention queue_rejects=12 kv_cache_hit=0.41 p99=432ms
2026-03-14T03:12:24Z route=northbridge-dedicated batch_formed=2 batch_wait_ms=60 kernel=fallback_matmul queue_rejects=9 kv_cache_hit=0.38 p99=398ms
```
We also saw many small batches (<=4) which is odd given typical load.

dylan: Thanks. Initial read: small batches + increased batch_wait_ms suggests we're timing out waiting for more tokens and falling back to slower kernels. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~40% vs normal ~72% — that lines up with more cold starts and smaller kv cache reuse.

priya: Noted. There's also a kernel-selector change that landed on 2026-02-10 which we suspected might be slightly more conservative and picks a generic attention kernel for certain sequence-length combos. We saw a small regression in canaries then but it didn't trigger rollbacks. Might be contributing.

dylan: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) increase per-route token_budget so worker batching can aggregate more tokens before hitting the budget, 2) raise queue_limit for northbridge queue so we don't reject as many inflight requests, 3) temporarily relax kernel-selector threshold to prefer fused kernels for 1-2 days while we canary a fix. My concrete numbers: token_budget -> `200000` tokens, queue_limit -> `120` (was 64), and reduce `batch_wait_ms` to 40ms for this route.

priya: Follow-up: I recommend we canary the kernel-selector delta to 10% traffic and keep the token_budget/queue_limit increase global for the route (48h). If we see no regressions, escalate to 50% then full. Also enable KV prefetch for this route to boost cache hit-rate.

joseph: Caution on memory: increasing token_budget increases KV memory pressure on Dedicated-XL workers. I checked capacity and we have ~18% headroom but need per-rt caps. I'll add a soft cap per-worker: `rt_token_cap=300k` to avoid OOMs. I'll also add a prom alert for `kv_mem_usage > 75%` on this pool.

samira (nb-support): Customer is OK with a 48h canary and the higher limits. They require we meet p99 < 250ms post-change. Is that realistic?

dylan: If kernel-selector reverts to fused kernels for the hot path and KV hit-rate recovers with prefetch, p99 should be back under 250ms. We'll monitor closely.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: starting canary rollout -> route: northbridge-dedicated, canary_pct=10, token_budget=220000, queue_limit=120, batch_wait_ms=40. Rolling out now :rocket:

perf-bot: perf-snapshot: https://perf.internal/redwood/snapshots/1795001234-northbridge-canary (profiling artifacts: kernel histograms, batch size distribution, kv-hit-rate)

samira (nb-support): Thanks everyone — I'll keep the customer updated and post any biz-side feedback here. Please paste perf updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
